LESSON: GRAFTING IN PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES
Topic 4.1: Grafting in plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grafting in plants, part of PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is grafting done on a plant?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grafting in plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Skill on reflection on own work as learners evaluate success on the grafted plant for rejuvenation,

aesthetics, repair or improvement of existing plant.

● Self-efficacy: Awareness of potential skills in manipulation of a plant through grafting for plant propagation.

Values:
• Respect: Appreciating each other’s abilities and skills as learners carry out grafting technique with varied degrees of

success.

• Responsibility: Taking assigned roles as learners undertake tasks in the grafting practical activity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety of self and others as learners handle and use sharp grafting tools and equipment.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learners relate carrying out grafting to parts of a plant and relationship between plants learnt in Integrated Science.
